objective:
Autonomous web research + structured markdown synthesis for a simultaneous multi-encode streaming pipeline on a DEDICATED STREAM-ONLY laptop. Save the report to b0ttsagent/temp/multi-encode-streaming-research.md. Verify claims with current web sources (prefer 2024-2026) and cite inline (URL + what each source establishes).

=== HARDWARE CONTEXT (stream-only laptop, runs NO games, only encodes) ===
- Lenovo IdeaPad Pro 5 16IMH9, Windows 11, plugged in, Best Performance power mode
- CPU: Intel Core Ultra 9 185H (16 cores; Quick Sync Video media engine supports H.264/HEVC/AV1 encode on Meteor Lake)
- iGPU: Intel Arc (owns the QSV encoder); dGPU: NVIDIA RTX 4050 Laptop (NVENC supports H.264/HEVC/AV1 encode; Ada AD107, single physical NVENC engine)
- RAM: 32GB LPDDR5x-7467 (soldered, shared with iGPU)
- Audio/multi-track recording already handled via NDI in their guide (brief note only)

=== SEPARATE GAMING PC (runs the games; NOT the laptop) ===
- i7-11700F + RTX 3060 + 32GB DDR4
- Sends video to the stream laptop via a Vixlw USB capture card (currently working at 1080p60). Alternative documented ingest exists: NDI Screen Capture HX (HEVC, GPU-accelerated) over Wi-Fi, one-to-many. See b0ttsagent/NavGuides/NdiStreamingNavGuide.md.

=== ENCODERS AVAILABLE IN OBS (user's exact list) ===
1. x264 (software/CPU), 2. QuickSync H.264, 3. QuickSync AV1, 4. QuickSync HEVC, 5. NVIDIA NVENC H.264, 6. NVIDIA NVENC H.264 "new", 7. NVIDIA NVENC HEVC.
NOTE: NVENC AV1 is NOT in their listed encoders. VERIFY whether RTX 4050 + current OBS Studio + StreamLabs Desktop expose NVENC AV1; do not assume. QSV AV1 is available.

=== THREE SIMULTANEOUS OUTPUTS THE LAPTOP PRODUCES ===
A) OBS (vanilla OBS Studio OR StreamLabs Desktop — USER ALTERNATES BETWEEN THEM, does NOT run both at once) streams RTMP to a self-hosted Prism multistream relay on a VPS over Tailscale; Prism fans out to Twitch/YouTube/Kick. HARD CONSTRAINT: Twitch ingest is H.264 ONLY, and the VPS relay path is safest as H.264, so the OBS-to-Prism LIVE feed must be H.264. Priority: HIGH.
B) Recording to disk (local file via OBS). Codec is free; HEVC or AV1 preferred for fidelity/size. Priority: LOWEST (user said if forced to trade off, keep both LIVES and skimp/drop recording).
C) TikTok Live Studio app -> live to TikTok. Separate standalone app with its own capture + encode. Priority: HIGH (equal to A).

=== NETWORK ===
~30 Mbps upload over Wi-Fi (close to a wired extender). Two upstreams simultaneously: OBS-to-Prism (~6 Mbps) + TikTok Live Studio (~4-6 Mbps). Compute feasibility against this.

=== CORE ARCHITECTURE QUESTION (DELIVER A DEFINITIVE RANKED RECOMMENDATION) ===
How to feed the SAME capture-card video to BOTH the main streaming app (OBS vanilla or StreamLabs) AND TikTok Live Studio simultaneously, given Windows UVC capture devices are typically exclusive-open (single opener). User currently uses OBS Fullscreen Projector (Source) to a window/monitor that TikTok then captures. Evaluate and rank these methods with pros/cons + cite sources:
1. OBS Virtual Camera -> TikTok Live Studio (OBS owns the card; enable Virtual Camera; TikTok Live Studio adds it as a camera/webcam source). VERIFY TikTok Live Studio supports virtual-camera input in CURRENT versions; cite the source and version/date.
2. SplitCam / vCam / vMix virtual-camera layers.
3. NDI as the ingest (replaces the card): NDI is one-to-many so multiple OBS-class apps can subscribe, BUT TikTok Live Studio has no NDI support so you still need OBS->Virtual Cam into TikTok. Verify whether DistroAV works in current StreamLabs Desktop (historically spotty) and whether OBS Virtual Cam + NDI coexist.
4. DirectShow multi-open / capture-card splitter filters for common cheap UVC cards (Vixlw-class) — investigate whether these cards allow multi-open at all.
5. The user's current Fullscreen Projector method — quantify the extra load/latency and explain why it's inferior to Virtual Camera.

ALSO state explicitly: since the user ALTERNATES vanilla OBS vs StreamLabs (never both at once), the capture-card contention between those TWO apps is moot — the only true simultaneous contention is (OBS) vs TikTok Live Studio.

=== TIKTOK LIVE STUDIO SPECIFICS (research + cite current docs) ===
- Does it support Virtual Camera / webcam sources? Game/Window/Display capture? Multi-source scenes? (confirm + cite)
- What encoder does TikTok Live Studio use internally — does the user choose it, or does it auto-select a hardware encoder (NVENC/QSV)? Can it be forced to RTX 4050 NVENC or Intel QSV? Can you disable its internal encoder and just pass through?
- Resolution/framerate caps by account tier (720p30 / 720p60 / 1080p30 / 1080p60) — how a user tells which tier they have.
- Recommended bitrate / keyframe / settings at each cap.

=== ENCODER SELECTION MATRIX (definitive pick per output with reasoning) ===
Key constraint to reason about: Ada AD107 has ONE physical NVENC engine, so running MULTIPLE NVENC encodes simultaneously SERIALIZES them (queued, higher latency, possible frame drops). The laptop has THREE independent encode engines available: NVENC (1 engine), QSV (Intel media engine, 1 engine), x264 (CPU, many threads). Since the laptop is stream-only, ALL engines are free. Recommend a split that avoids burning one engine for all ~3 encodes.
- OBS-to-Prism LIVE feed (must be H.264): pick among NVENC H.264 "new" vs QSV H.264 vs x264 — give the definitive choice for the priority-1 feed and justify (latency, stability, Twitch-tier quality). Provide exact values: rate control (CBR?), bitrate target anchored to Twitch-tier ~6000 Kbps unless evidence supports more, keyframe interval (2s for 60fps), preset, profile (High), tier, b-frames, lookahead, psycho-visual tuning.
- Recording: pick among NVENC HEVC vs QSV AV1 vs NVENC AV1 (if exposed) vs x264 slow — recommend for 1080p60 high fidelity (not for sharing). Provide exact values: CQ/VBR rate control, CQ level, bitrate ceiling, preset (P5/P6 NVENC or quality/best QSV), color range + color space (Rec.709, limited vs full), keyframe, and a one-line audio-multitrack note.
- TikTok Live Studio: report what it auto-uses; tell the user what to expect and any checkboxes to verify.
- Give a one-line ENCODER ASSIGNMENT SUMMARY like: "Prism live = NVENC H.264 new; Recording = QSV AV1 (or NVENC HEVC); TikTok = TikTok's internal (likely NVENC)." Justify the anti-contention split.

=== FEASIBILITY VERDICT ===
Can this EXACT hardware (Ultra 9 185H + RTX 4050, stream-only, free NVENC/QSV/CPU) simultaneously run: capture-card ingest + OBS record + OBS live-to-Prism + TikTok Live Studio live, stable at 1080p60 over 30 Mbps Wi-Fi? Answer YES / CONDITIONAL / NO with concrete caveats: thermal throttling risk on the IdeaPad Pro 5 16IMH9 cooling under sustained multi-encode; dual-GPU routing (game capture path must land on the dGPU); Wi-Fi variance; capture card sharing. Note explicitly that since the laptop renders no games, NVENC and QSV are fully available for encoding — this is the key feasibility enabler.

=== CONCRETE SETTINGS TABLES (ready to type) FOR BOTH APPS ===
Vanilla OBS Studio: Settings > Output > Advanced mode. Provide a Streaming block (encoder, rate control, bitrate, keyframe, preset, profile, tier, b-frames, tuning) and a Recording block (different encoder than streaming, CQ, preset, color) and an Audio tab note (multitrack). Provide both Simple AND Advanced output guidance as relevant.
StreamLabs Desktop (SLOBS): CRITICAL — verify and report whether CURRENT StreamLabs Desktop lets you set a DIFFERENT encoder for RECORDING vs STREAMING (historically SLOBS Simple output used ONE encoder for both; only Replay Buffer / dedicated-recording workflows allowed a second encoder). Give the exact current UI path to achieve independent stream vs record encoders in SLOBS, or state clearly if it is NOT possible and give the best fallback (e.g., same encoder for both, or use vanilla OBS for the record+live combo). Cite a current source for SLOBS encoder behavior.
Per-game bitrate hints (Minecraft / Fortnite / Roblox): mainly motion/bitrate tuning + keyframe notes (Fortnite high motion may need higher bitrate or lower game fps target). Since all three are captured from the card identically, note any game-specific adjustments.

=== REPORT FORMAT ===
Top: one-line TL;DR with the recommended architecture + encoder assignments. Then ordered sections matching above. Include a Risks/Gotchas section (capture card exclusive-open, SLOBS single-encoder caveat, TikTok autonomously choosing encoder, Prism VPS RTMP destination regenerates on restart, Wi-Fi variance, thermal). End with exact-to-paste settings for vanilla OBS AND StreamLabs. Keep it dense and practical, not hand-wavy.
summary:
# Research: Simultaneous Multi-Encode Streaming Pipeline (Dedicated Stream Laptop)

> **TL;DR** — Let the streaming app (vanilla OBS **or** StreamLabs, never both) own the Vixlw capture card and output **H.264 1080p60 CBR 6000 Kbps via NVENC H.264 (new)** to the Prism relay; record locally with **QSV AV1 (ICQ ~20-22, Target Usage: Quality)** on the Intel media engine; feed TikTok Live Studio through **OBS Virtual Camera** (TikTok has no NDI and cannot share the UVC card) and let TikTok's internal encoder auto-select (expect hardware NVENC/QSV). This splits the three encodes across two independent hardware engines + one auto engine. Verdict: **CONDITIONAL YES** — the three engines are all free because this laptop renders no games; the caveats are Wi-Fi variance, chassis thermals, and updating both apps so the modern encoder lists (incl. NVENC AV1) are exposed.

---

## 1. Core architecture — how to feed the same capture-card video to BOTH apps

**Explicit statement first:** because you alternate vanilla OBS Studio and StreamLabs Desktop (never simultaneously), capture-card contention between *those two* is moot. The only true simultaneous contention is **streaming-app vs TikTok Live Studio**, and that is solved 100% by making the streaming app the single owner of the card and handing TikTok a virtual camera stream. The Windows UVC/DirectShow model is exclusive-open for generic devices, so only one process may open the Vixlw card at a time — verified: DirectShow webcams are exclusive-use resources and apps throw "camera is already in use" on second open ([StackOverflow, DirectShow exclusive capture](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/28605444/two-instances-from-one-webcam)); multi-app sharing is a *special vendor feature* that only certain Elgato devices implement, not a generic UVC capability ([Elgato KB — Multi App Support](https://help.elgato.com/hc/en-us/articles/360042392672-Elgato-Capture-Devices-and-Multi-App-Support)).
